conf.description: AWS GovCloud CloudTrail data-events / eventbridge direct route: strip the EventBridge envelope and extract the ECS anchors directly in Cribl, then DROP the record (no _raw snapshot) per recommendations.direct.cribl's volume/low-forensic-value tradeoff for this dataset - overrides the field table's aws.cloudtrail.flattened.detail custom target, which management-events keeps but this dataset does not

conf.comment: EventBridge delivers one S3/Lambda data-event per message under detail{}. Object-level volume is 1-3 orders of magnitude above management events with far lower per-record forensic value (dataset description), and recommendations.direct.cribl says explicitly to 'drop _raw first' rather than keep the audit-of-last-resort copy management-events keeps. So this pipeline extracts the given ECS anchors itself (file.path/file.name split, faas.name, event.action/provider, cloud.account.id from the in-record recipientAccountId) and then discards detail/_raw entirely - there is no downstream record left for anything else to re-parse.

functions.description: Pipeline purpose and the deliberate no-_raw, extract-only design (per recommendations.direct.cribl)
Parse the EventBridge envelope and native data-event record under detail{} from _raw JSON

Computed fields read from ORIGINAL vendor names before rename: 'detail-type' needs bracket access (hyphen), and the S3 object key is split into file.path (full key, per the field row's ecs target) and file.name (last slash-delimited segment, per the field row's own note) since no dedicated split function exists on the whitelist
_time from the in-record data-plane completion time (genuinely nested path, not a flat dotted key) - never @timestamp

Batch rename of the clean envelope fields and the clean nested detail.* ECS anchors. As with management-events, cloud.account.id comes from the in-record recipientAccountId, never the envelope's own 'account' (which this dataset's field table does not even list, unlike management-events, so it is not extracted at all here)

event.dataset (no hyphen) and cleanup: drop the now-partially-mutated 'detail' object, the hyphenated envelope key via glob, and _raw itself per recommendations.direct.cribl's explicit 'drop _raw first' instruction for this high-volume, low-forensic-value dataset - the extracted fields above are all this pipeline forwards
